lessons.title: Work and study plans
objectives: Describe a work or study plan using clear future language.
Use a main idea and one relevant detail in a response about describing a work goal.

content_sections.title: Notice form and meaning (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Read the model aloud twice: 'I am going to apply for a part-time job after I finish my course.' Underline the words that show the situation, time, or result. In this lesson, describe a work or study plan using clear future language. Keep the language connected: do not give isolated words.

content_sections.title: Guided dialogue (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Partner A begins a realistic exchange about describing a work goal. Partner B asks for one missing detail. Swap roles and make one change to the time, place, reason, quantity, or next action. Check that the exchange achieves: Describe a work or study plan using clear future language.

content_sections.title: Independent response (6 minutes)
content_sections.body: Create a short message about describing a work goal without reading the model. Include a main event or plan and one precise detail. Speak it once slowly, then once at a natural pace. Listen for whether the key information is clear.

exercises.prompt: Choose the response that gives a clear, useful message for this situation: describing a work goal.
options: I am going to apply for a part-time job after I finish my course.
That sounds good, but could we meet a little later?
Yesterday I felt ill, visited the clinic, and followed the nurse's advice.
exercises.correct_answer: I am going to apply for a part-time job after I finish my course.

exercises.prompt: Complete the model with the missing words: 'I am going to apply for a part-time job after I ____.'
Read this short message for the lesson 'Work and study plans' and identify the real-life situation it describes.
exercises.stimulus: I am going to apply for a part-time job after I finish my course. The message gives one main point and one detail for the listener.

questions.question: What situation does the message describe?
acceptable_answers: The message is about describing a work goal.

exercises.prompt: Speak for 30–45 seconds about describing a work goal. State the main message, add a relevant detail, and answer one follow-up question.

criteria: Communicates the main message about describing a work goal clearly.
Adds a relevant detail and responds appropriately to a follow-up question.

listening.instruction: Listen once to a short message about describing a work goal. Answer the question before the transcript is revealed, then listen again and check the key detail.
listening.goal: Identify the situation and a useful detail in a short message about describing a work goal.
listening.transcript: I am going to apply for a part-time job after I finish my course.
listening.question: What is the message mainly about?
listening.answer: The listener should understand that it concerns describing a work goal.
constraints: Keep the transcript private before the learner answers the first question.
Use only the supplied transcript; do not require media.

speaking.instruction: Roleplay describing a work goal. Learner role: explain the situation and give one useful detail. Tutor role: be a helpful listener, ask one specific follow-up, and confirm the next step. Begin with a natural greeting and finish once both roles agree on the next action.
speaking.goal: Complete a clear, practical exchange about describing a work goal.
constraints: Name the learner and tutor roles before the first turn.
Use at most three tutor turns and stop after the agreed next step.

pronunciation.instruction: Say the model for describing a work goal in two thought groups. Mark the pause between ideas, then stress the word that gives the key action, time, quantity, reason, or request. Record a second attempt after listening to your first attempt.
pronunciation.goal: Make the key information in describing a work goal easy to hear.
pronunciation.target: Thought-group pause and key-word stress in work and study plans
constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is supplied.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when learner audio is unavailable.

writing.instruction: Write a 35–50 word message about describing a work goal. Include the main event or plan, one precise detail, and the next action or response. Submit your own draft before requesting feedback.
writing.goal: Write a connected, useful short message about describing a work goal.
constraints: Wait for the learner draft before giving feedback.
Give concise feedback only; do not replace the learner draft.

lessons.title: Review: work, routines, and achievements
objectives: Review planning, achievement, and follow-up language.
Use a main idea and one relevant detail in a response about reviewing work and study language.

content_sections.title: Recall and select (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Work without notes first. For the situation 'reviewing work and study language', say one sentence that meets this goal: Review planning, achievement, and follow-up language. Then check the model: 'I can talk about a goal, an achievement, and a change to a plan.' Identify one word or phrase that makes the message clear.

content_sections.title: Compare two responses (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Give one clear response for reviewing work and study language, then ask a partner one follow-up question. Compare the response with the model and repair one missing time, reason, place, quantity, or next step. Use the whole unit's familiar language rather than memorising one sentence.

content_sections.title: Self-check and transfer (6 minutes)
content_sections.body: Before the unit test, check three things: the main message is clear, one useful detail is included, and the listener knows what happens next. Say or write a new short message about a similar situation, not the model about reviewing work and study language.
